canonical_definition: Across the provided literature, the dominant framing of Perplexity is as a quantitative metric for evaluating language model outputs, though a distinct minority of papers use the name to refer to a commercial LLM search engine. In its most common usage as a measurement, it is operationalized to assess various aspects of text quality, such as fluency, coherence, and naturalness, with one paper describing it as a "lightweight proxy for naturalness" ("CTCC: A Robust and Stealthy Fingerprinting Framework for Large Language Models via Cross-Turn Contextual Correlation Backdoor"). This general application is reflected in its use to measure constructs like Utility preservation, Faithfulness, and Imperceptibility. The evaluation procedure is sometimes specified as using a larger language model to calculate the perplexity of text generated by a smaller one. Beyond general quality assessment, Perplexity is also adapted into more specialized methods, including a "Perplexity Score" baseline for detecting pre-training data exposure and "sequence perplexity" as a value probing technique. In contrast, a smaller set of work treats "Perplexity" as a proper noun, identifying it as one of the "production LLM search engines" used as a target for evaluation.
